LUNA: The Shadow Dust is a beautiful point and click adventure game about climbing up a tower with your little cat-creature-companion to try and piece together what happened (wow you have amnesia) before reaching the top and restoring light to a world shrouded in darkness. LUNA has some great somber, heartfelt, exciting, mystical, and mysterious harp, orchestral, choral and piano ballads that provide a rich soundscape to back up the wonderful artstyle. The game of course also makes use of one of my favorite point and click puzzle games mechanics of making the music slowly build as you solve the puzzle in each room. LUNA's world is brimming with secrets proven by many of the achievements. Luna is also full of murals or frescos that light up as you solve various puzzles that make good use of the two characters you inhabit along the journey. Also of note is that LUNA has some animated cutscenes interspersed throughout the game that tell the vague, nonverbal tale and show a bit more action and drama than the standard point and click gameplay. The rooms and each of their puzzles were creative and interesting with concepts from cooking to seasonal time manipulation to one of the game's central mechanics: having the catlike-creature traverse the room in the shadows; this is reminiscent of Contrast from 2013 by Compulsion Games. Overall LUNA as a package is well made with each aspect hitting the mark, and enough variety and creativity complementing the beautiful music and animation to make this a worthy purchase when on sale.

One of the first games I played in this new gamer chapter of my life, and it completely blew me right out of the water with its gorgeous story and beautiful visuals. The puzzles are not difficult at all with a couple of exceptions.

The art and--especially--the music are out-of-this-world good. Like a Studio Ghibli film brought to game. The point-and-click nature of the puzzles might have been a little tedious without them, but they MORE than made up for any awkward mechanics or figuring what *precisely* can be interacted with. If you're into puzzles for their mechanical cleverness and intricacy, this won't satisfy that. But if you want a cozy vibe with all the feels and working on a few small puzzles along the way, this is your game.

LUNA The Shadow Dust is a hand-drawn puzzle adventure developed by Lantern Studio and published by Coconut Island Games together with Application Systems Heidelberg. The game distinguishes itself immediately through its commitment to visual storytelling and traditional animation, presenting an experience that feels closer to an interactive animated film than a conventional video game. Instead of relying on dialogue or written text to convey its narrative, the story unfolds entirely through expressive animation, environmental details, and symbolic imagery. This wordless approach creates a universal storytelling style that allows players from any background to interpret the journey through emotion, atmosphere, and visual clues.

The adventure begins with a mysterious boy named Üri who awakens in an unfamiliar landscape beside a massive tower that stretches far into the sky. With no clear memory of how he arrived there, the boy begins climbing the tower in search of answers. Early in the journey he encounters a strange black creature named Layh, whose cat-like appearance and curious behavior make it both a companion and an essential partner in the boy’s quest. From that moment onward, the two characters work together to navigate the tower’s intricate interior. Their partnership gradually becomes the emotional center of the story, as the two rely on each other to overcome obstacles and uncover the secrets hidden within the tower.

Gameplay revolves around exploring a series of rooms inside the towering structure, each presenting its own set of puzzles and mechanisms. Players frequently switch between controlling Üri and Layh, using their different abilities to interact with the environment. Üri can manipulate physical objects, climb structures, and activate certain mechanisms, while Layh possesses abilities that allow it to interact with shadows or reach areas that the boy cannot access. This dual-character mechanic encourages players to think about how each character’s actions affect the environment and how their abilities can complement one another to solve complex puzzles.

Many of the puzzles in LUNA The Shadow Dust rely heavily on observation and experimentation rather than explicit instructions. The game rarely tells players what to do, instead presenting rooms filled with mysterious machinery, symbols, and moving elements that must be understood through trial and error. Some puzzles involve manipulating shadows cast by objects or rearranging pieces of the environment so that Layh can traverse shadow paths to reach otherwise inaccessible locations. Others require players to coordinate both characters’ actions across different areas of a room, gradually unlocking new pathways through careful planning and timing.

The tower itself acts almost like a character within the story. Each floor introduces new visual themes and puzzle concepts, giving the sense that the structure contains layers of forgotten history and symbolism. Murals, statues, and environmental storytelling elements hint at a deeper narrative that gradually unfolds as players ascend higher into the tower. These visual clues help piece together the story behind the world and the characters without ever breaking the game’s silent storytelling style.

One of the most remarkable aspects of the game is its visual presentation. Every scene in LUNA The Shadow Dust is crafted using hand-drawn animation that gives the world a rich, painterly appearance. Characters move with expressive gestures and subtle details that convey emotion without the need for spoken dialogue. The environments are equally detailed, filled with intricate architecture, symbolic imagery, and lighting effects that create a magical atmosphere. The animation quality often resembles traditional animated films, which helps the game maintain a strong visual identity throughout the entire adventure.

The soundtrack plays an equally important role in shaping the emotional tone of the game. Because the narrative unfolds without dialogue, music becomes one of the primary tools used to convey mood and tension. Soft piano melodies accompany moments of quiet exploration, while more dramatic orchestral pieces emerge during key story moments. The music guides the player’s emotional journey through the tower, reinforcing the sense of wonder, mystery, and occasional melancholy that defines the experience.

The pacing of the game is intentionally slow and contemplative. Rather than focusing on action or fast progression, LUNA The Shadow Dust encourages players to observe their surroundings and appreciate the details of the world. This calm rhythm allows players to immerse themselves fully in the atmosphere of the tower while gradually solving its puzzles. The journey feels more like a thoughtful exploration than a race to reach the ending, which fits well with the game’s reflective storytelling style.

However, the game’s design may present challenges for some players. Because puzzles rely heavily on environmental observation and provide little guidance, certain sections can become confusing if players overlook a key visual clue. Unlike many modern puzzle games, there is no hint system to provide assistance when players become stuck. This design choice emphasizes discovery and experimentation, but it can occasionally lead to moments of frustration for those unfamiliar with traditional point-and-click puzzle logic.

Another limitation is the relatively short length of the adventure. Most players will complete the journey within three to four hours, depending on how quickly they solve the puzzles. While the shorter runtime helps maintain a focused experience without unnecessary filler, it may leave some players wishing for additional chapters within this beautifully crafted world.

Despite its brevity, LUNA The Shadow Dust leaves a lasting impression thanks to its artistic ambition and emotional storytelling. The relationship between Üri and Layh, combined with the mysterious nature of the tower and its symbolic imagery, creates a journey that feels both personal and mythic. The absence of dialogue allows players to project their own interpretations onto the story, making the experience feel uniquely personal.

Ultimately, LUNA The Shadow Dust stands as an excellent example of how video games can function as a form of visual storytelling. By blending traditional animation with puzzle design and environmental narrative, the game creates an experience that feels timeless and deeply atmospheric. It may not offer the longest adventure or the most complex mechanics, but its artistry, creativity, and emotional resonance make it a memorable journey for anyone willing to climb the tower and discover its secrets.

Rating: 9/10

[h2][url=store.steampowered.com/app/465100/LUNA_The_Shadow_Dust/]LUNA: The Shadow Dust[/url]'s wholesome charm emanates from its exceptionally evocative art style.[/h2]

Climb an impressive tower with a friend, where each floor is a self-contained challenge, until later where floors involve multiple scenes, usually with a clue on the wall to indicate what must be done to unlock the next room and move on.

Puzzles are fairly straightforward, except for a few that unfortunately felt convoluted and left a mildly disappointing mark. At least one section requires precise timing, another towards the end requires remembering a clock face time on a previous level, easy to overlook.

The game would earn more praise with a better balanced sense of logic, but is nevertheless highly recommendable.

[h3]Positive[/h3]
[list]

[*] Contemplative puzzles, largely straightforward (only rarely unintuitive)
[*] Beautiful traditional animation cutscenes
[*] Highly pleasant soundtrack
[*] Alternate between characters
[*] Ending makes sense of the beginning and gives purpose to the journey
[/list]

[h3]Negative[/h3]
[list]
[*] Full ending only available after finding difficult to discover secret island
[*] Mismatched difficulty and irregular logic on a few specific puzzles
[/list]

Игра очень милая и трогательная, оставляет приятные и теплые впечатления, а концовка заставит плакать, если вы конечно сентиментальны. В этой игре нет никакого словесного повествования, но от этого она не менее замечательная, а напротив глубина сюжета наполнена драматизмом, ярким приключением и все это удается прочувствовать за счет кат-сцен. История показана в обратном порядке и в конце даст полную картину, но все же некоторые детали умалчивают и их можно додумать. Визуально красивая прорисовка, успокаивающее музыкальное сопровождение, которое заставляет полностью погрузиться и насладиться процессом. Головоломки увлекательные и в целом не сложные, они интуитивно понятные. Интерфейс сведён к минимуму, поэтому все скрыто в причудливых интерьерах, а каждая комната это отдельная загадка. Также понравилось еще переключение между героями для более эффективного распределения задач. Из минусов нет возможности мгновенной выйти из комнаты по клику на дверь, а так главный персонаж медленно перемещается прогулочным шагом к двери
✔️Стоит играть, если вы сентиментальны и любите трогательные и глубокие эмоциональные истории в сказочном стиле, всем любителям качественных point-and-click игр, а также тем, кто ищите игру для спокойного и уютного вечера
✖️Не понравится, если вас раздражает неторопливое прохождение или не любите головоломки

当初是和漫长等待一起捆绑买的，先去玩漫长等待了，这个一直搁置到最近才玩。

本作最让我惊讶的点在于一个2h流程的游戏，竟设置有隐藏结局。是一个中外共同合作的小成本游戏。评价是好看＞好玩，整体给个7.5分。
美术绝对是游戏木桶最长的那一块，全部使用手绘，设计了一个架空的神秘文明。动画也都是12帧逐帧动画，有着20分钟的过场动画。使用风格化符号和未知文字代替了文本和对话，这对叙事水平提高了要求，也为背景故事蒙上一层神秘色彩。

故事比较隐晦，主要通过没有文字的（和读不懂的文字）图像和过场动画说明，如果像我一样，不看游戏页介绍直接进入游玩，那么在前期你真的不知道主角的目的、主角的身份。直到后期剧情集中爆发才能管中窥豹知晓些许。所以建议先看一下游戏介绍。

主要玩法是指向点击解谜，较为简单，虽说是双主角设计——一人一小“怪兽”，但其实大部分工作可以由人完成，部分情节为了分担解谜工作给小怪兽而限制人的行为很反直觉、很出戏。比如小猫可以爬上梯子但人不行。
另外一个问题是作为一个指向点击解谜游戏，可互动的物品和提示并没有在视觉上很好的凸显出来，而是以画面整体性为第一位，这导致部分以图像为线索的关卡会卡关、部分关卡需要花一定时间判断是否能互动。

最后，作为成就党，成就设置的并不好，有无意义的重复劳动。

Weird setting and puzzles in [b]Luna[/b]: The Shadow Night, truly achieve that fairytale book feel.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Point and click puzzle game where you control two characters, each able to do something the other can’t, and occasionally gameplay sections are interrupted by short cutscenes that drive the story forward.

[h1]Story[/h1]
Something about darkness and protecting who you love, the game isn’t exactly clear with the details as it doesn’t feature any sort of language to make this little tale as far reaching as possible.

[h1]X-Factor[/h1]
Certainly its aesthetics, it looks as a children’s fairytales book.

[h1]Downsides[/h1]
Moonman logic in puzzle games is only good if it makes humor of its absurdity, and no humor is found here José, on top of that many puzzles are tedious due to either repetitiveness of tasks or controls not properly registering making you mess up the execution and do the puzzle from the beginning.

The title features a beautiful ending cutscene, how is it a bad thing?
The ending cutscene alone contains more than double the artwork than the rest of the game, either this was an animation haphazardly turned into a game at the last second or a gross mismanagement of resources.
The worst offender here is how the two characters that you’ll see always on screen have only a couple of frames of choppy game animations compared to maybe minute things that get much better treatment.

画风不错，很治愈。游戏性很差，重复性解密太多了，一个同样的解密思路，它敢让你重复四次。动画挺好看，但是剧情有点老套，感觉像是逆徒篡位，主角让人喜欢不起来。

Interessant, jetzt wo ich das Spiel durch habe und ein wenig dazu gelesen, erfahre ich, das die Hauptfigur ein Junge sein soll. Für mich war es das ganze Spiel über ein Mädchen. 

Zur Geschichte an sich kann ich nicht viel schreiben, denn so richtig begriffen habe ich sie wohl nicht. Ein Kind, ein Turm, Licht und Schatten, Erinnerungen, Bedrohung einer Welt, ein Superheld in Katzengestalt. Also selbst spielen und sich eigene Gedanken dazu machen. 

Die Grafik im Spiel ist sehr schön anzusehen. Harmonische Farben und Formen. Die Musik dazu ist passend. Geheimnisvoll, mystisch, traurig-dramatisch - je nachdem, was die Figuren erleben. 

Besonders positiv empfand ich, dass es hier keine Dialoge gab. Wie herrlich, kein Gequatsche durch das man sich endlos klicken muss. Wobei so manche Gesprächsfetzen in anderen Spielen durchaus inspirierend oder humorvoll sind. Aber hier gab es ausnahmsweise mal erholsame Stille. Nur die Musik erzählte. Und natürlich die Bilder.

Die Rätsel im Spiel fand ich im ersten Teil sehr schön. Im zweiten Teil ein wenig anstrengend. Insgesamt hat es aber Spaß gemacht. 

Nicht ganz so optimal fand ich - mal wieder, ich weiß - die langsame Bewegungsgeschwindigkeit (die hier dann durchaus doppelt vorkommt, da man abwechselnd zwei Charaktere steuert). Und auch, dass man nicht etwas anklicken konnte, um die Figur dorthin zu schicken, sondern es ging nur durch Zwischenschritte. Figur befindet sich auf einer Leiter? Also muss sie erst absteigen (Klick neben die Leiter), dann kann sie woandershin gehen (Klick auf das nächste Ziel). Die Figur befindet sich in einem Gefährt? Also muss sie erst aussteigen (klick), dann kann man ihr das nächste Ziel geben (klick). Das hätte etwas komfortabler gelöst werden können (Figur steht auf der Leiter? Man klickt das nächste Ziel an und sie geht einfach dorthin). 

Auch mussten manche Dinge wieder und wieder wiederholt werden (das Holen der Bücher in der Bibliothek z.b.). Trotz dieser Bremsen, empfand ich das Spiel als spannend genug (außerdem künstlerisch sehr schön), um es bis zum Ende schaffen zu wollen. Die Laufwege waren auch immer kurz und die meiste Zeit auf nur einen Raum bezogen. Also durchaus Daumen hoch.

[b]Luna: The Shadow Dust[/b] é uma obra-prima indie do gênero Point and Click, que nos convida a explorar uma misteriosa torre enquanto controlamos dois personagens complementares: Luna e uma estranha criatura que lembra um cachorro. Combinando cooperação e habilidade, eles resolvem quebra-cabeças em cada andar para avançar na história.

[h2]Aspectos Visuais e Imersão[/h2]
O jogo é um espetáculo visual. Cada cenário foi desenhado à mão com um traço belíssimo, criando um ambiente mágico e unico. As animações fluem suavemente, enriquecendo ainda mais a experiência imersiva. Este é, sem dúvida, um dos pontos mais fortes do jogo. 

[h2]História e Temática[/h2]
Ao iniciar, parecia apenas um passatempo relaxante, mas rapidamente a narrativa cativante me surpreendeu. Sem palavras, o jogo transmite emoções intensas e mensagens profundas. A jornada na torre pode ser vista como uma metáfora para a superação de dores, fracassos e memórias difíceis. Como em Gris, Luna é um mergulho em cores, sons e sensações, evocando uma luta contra sentimentos como solidão e depressão. É uma experiência emocionante.

[h2]Jogabilidade e Puzzles[/h2]
Os puzzles são acessíveis, criativos e muito prazerosos de resolver. Não são desafiadores ao ponto de frustrar, mas envolvem o jogador de forma satisfatória. 

[h2]Preço e Valor[/h2]
O preço pode parecer elevado, mas é perceptível o cuidado e a paixão que os desenvolvedores colocaram no projeto. Para quem prefere economizar, vale ficar atento a promoções, mas posso afirmar que a qualidade justifica o investimento.

[h2]Trilha Sonora[/h2]
A trilha sonora é uma obra-prima à parte. As músicas complementam perfeitamente os cenários, intensificando o impacto emocional de cada momento.


[b]Cada enigma é um sussurro de solidão; cada andar, uma memória pintada à mão. A torre é mais que uma construção: é um reflexo da alma, uma metáfora para a ascensão árdua em busca de significado. Luna: The Shadow Dust não entrega respostas, mas nos lembra que há beleza em continuar, mesmo quando tudo parece perdido.[/b]

[h2]Avaliação Geral:[/h2]

Visual: 10/10
História: 10/10
Puzzles: 10/10
Preço: 7/10
Trilha sonora: 10/10

[b]Recomendo para quem busca uma experiência poética, imersiva e tocante.[/b]

Cada enigma é um sussurro de solidão, cada cenário, uma memória pintada à mão. A torre, com seus andares que se perdem na penumbra, é mais que uma construção: é um reflexo da alma, uma metáfora para a ascensão árdua em busca de sentido no vazio. Sem palavras, o jogo nos fala da dualidade: a luz que se esconde na escuridão, o silêncio que revela verdades profundas. LUNA The Shadow Dust é um poema interativo que não oferece respostas, mas nos lembra que, por mais perdida que pareça a jornada, sempre há beleza no ato de seguir em frente, um passo de cada vez...
